job.title: Clinical Trials Manager
job.description:
On Q are proud to partner with an innovative Australian biotechnology organisation developing breakthrough therapies designed to address serious global health challenges. With an active Phase III clinical trial currently underway, we are seeking a hands-on Clinical Trials Manager to lead operational delivery across Australia and support activities in Asia-Pacific.
  
 
This is an exciting opportunity to join a lean, agile team where you will have direct visibility across all aspects of trial execution and the ability to make a genuine impact on study outcomes.
  
 
The Opportunity
Reporting to the Head of Clinical Operations, you will be responsible for overseeing the day-to-day management of a Phase III clinical trial in Australia, including site engagement, recruitment performance, monitoring activities and vendor oversight. You will also support the coordination and oversight of local partners and sites in the Asia-Pacific region.
   
Key Responsibilities
 
  • Drive operational delivery of an active clinical trial
  • Conduct site monitoring visits and maintain strong site engagement
  • Monitor recruitment performance and implement strategies to support enrolment targets
  • Oversee local partners, CROs, vendors and service providers
  • Ensure compliance with GCP, study protocols and regulatory requirements
  • Maintain study documentation, trial management systems and inspection readiness
   

This role will suit a proactive, self-sufficient clinical professional who enjoys remaining close to sites and operational delivery rather than managing large teams.
  
 
About You
To be successful, you will bring: 
  • Solid years' experience within Clinical Research as a Senior CRA, Clinical Trials Manager, Clinical Project Manager or similar role
  • Experience supporting or managing late-stage and/or Phase III clinical trials
  • Strong site management and monitoring experience
  • Strong knowledge of ICH-GCP and Australian clinical trial requirements
  • Experience overseeing CROs, vendors and external partners
  • Experience within biotech, startup or emerging pharmaceutical environments is advantageous
  
 
What's on Offer?
 
  • Broad exposure across trial management, site engagement and international operations
  • Opportunity to work directly with senior leadership
  • Hybrid working environment (3 in SYD office / 2 WFH)
  • Travel to investigator sites within Australia and periodic Asia-Pacific travel (approx. every two months, dependent on trial requirements)
   

If you're seeking an opportunity to join an innovative and growing biotechnology environment, we'd love to hear from you.

job.title: ANZ Quality Director
job.description:
Are you an experienced quality leader who thrives in complex manufacturing environments and enjoys balancing strategic leadership with operational excellence?

We are seeking an ANZ Quality Director to lead quality strategy, governance, and performance across a multi-site manufacturing network in Australia and New Zealand. This newly created leadership position has been established to strengthen regional quality capability, support future growth initiatives, and provide dedicated oversight across multiple regulated manufacturing operations.

The Opportunity

Reporting into global quality leadership, the ANZ Quality Director will provide strategic oversight across multiple manufacturing sites while supporting significant transformation projects, quality system improvements, and organisational development initiatives. 
You will work closely with site leadership teams, serving as a trusted partner and advisor on quality, compliance, business performance, and continuous improvement. This position requires a leader who can operate autonomously, influence at senior levels, and confidently make decisions that support both compliance and commercial outcomes.

Key Responsibilities 
  • Act as the lead quality authority for Australia and New Zealand.
  • Develop and execute regional quality strategy aligned with business objectives.
  • Drive continuous improvement initiatives and identify opportunities to streamline processes and improve efficiency.
  • Lead quality planning activities across multiple manufacturing sites
  • Provide oversight of quality operations across biologics, pharmaceutical and other regulated manufacturing activities.
  • Lead quality involvement in major site transformation and capability expansion projects.
  • Lead, coach and develop site quality leaders across the ANZ network.
  • Build a culture of  ownership and high performance.
  • Develop future leadership talent and succession pipelines.
To be considered for this role, you will have the following qualifications and skills:
  • Extensive quality leadership experience within pharmaceutical, biologics, biotechnology, animal health, medical device or similarly regulated manufacturing environments.
  • Proven experience leading quality teams across multiple sites or regions.
  • Strong understanding of GMP, quality systems, regulatory compliance and inspection readiness.
  • Demonstrated success leading organisational change, quality transformation or large-scale improvement initiatives.
  • Experience managing complex stakeholder relationships and influencing at executive level.
  • Strong commercial acumen and the ability to align quality outcomes with broader business objectives.
  • A track record of developing teams, managing performance and building leadership capability.
This is a rare opportunity to step into a highly influential role where you will act as the senior quality authority for the region, partnering with executive stakeholders to shape long-term strategy while building a high-performing and accountable quality organisation. For a confidential conversation about this role, please email Grace Bitodi at gbitodi@onqrecruitment.com.au.

job.title: Analytical Chemist
job.description:
Join an innovative Australian medical technology company developing breakthrough cancer surgery solutions that have the potential to improve patient outcomes worldwide. Working as part of a close-knit and highly collaborative team, you will play a key role in supporting the development, scale-up and manufacture of a novel nanoparticle-based technology currently progressing through clinical trials and towards commercialisation. 

This is a unique opportunity for an analytical chemist who enjoys variety and wants to work across analytical testing, method development, manufacturing support, quality control and product development in a fast-paced environment. 

 
About the Role

You will support analytical development and characterisation activities across research, manufacturing and quality operations.

Key responsibilities include:
  • Developing, transferring and validating analytical methods to support product development and regulatory programmes 
  • Performing analytical characterisation of polymers, magnetic nanoparticles and related materials. 
  • Conducting routine and non-routine testing to support R&D, manufacturing and batch release activities. 
  • Operating, maintaining, calibrating and qualifying laboratory instrumentation. 
  • Supporting GMP laboratory activities, SOP development and quality system compliance.  
  • Analysing data and preparing technical reports, certificates of analysis and documentation for regulatory submissions. 
  • Coordinating testing activities with external laboratories and service providers. 
  • Contributing across multiple projects as the business transitions from clinical development towards commercialisation and manufacturing scale-up. 
About You

To be considered for this role, you will have the following skills and qualifications: 
  • MSc or PhD qualifications in Chemistry, Analytical Chemistry or a related discipline. 
  • Experience working within regulated laboratory environments, ideally GMP, pharmaceutical, biotechnology or medical device settings. 
  • Strong hands-on HPLC experience is essential. 
  • Experience in analytical method development and/or quality control.
  • Strong trouble-shooting skills. 
  • Excellent data interpretation and problem-solving skills
  • Exposure to techniques such as NMR, ICP-MS, ICP-OES will be highly regarded. 
  • A collaborative mindset and willingness to contribute across R&D, manufacturing support and quality activities. 
Why Join?
  • Be part of a company developing cutting-edge cancer surgery technology.
  • Gain exposure across R&D, analytical development, manufacturing and quality functions. 
  • Work alongside passionate scientists and engineers in a highly collaborative environment where ideas are valued and contributions have a direct impact. 
  • Join a growing organisation at a pivotal stage of product development and commercialisation. 
If you are looking for a role where you can apply your analytical expertise while contributing to the development of life-changing medical technology, we would love to hear from you. For a confidential conversation about the role, please email Grace Bitodi, gbitodi@onqrecruitment.com.au.

job.title: Quality and Technical Specialist
job.description:
Are you a quality professional who thrives on accuracy, compliance, and technical documentation?

Our client is a family-owned organisation specialising in premium complementary medicine and functional food ingredients across Australia and New Zealand. Recognised for the quality of their ingredients and industry-leading technical documentation, they partner with some of the region's most recognised health and wellness brands. As the business continues to grow, they are seeking a Quality & Technical Specialist to join their Scientific Affairs team. 

This is an excellent opportunity for someone who enjoys vendor assurance, raw material assessment, quality systems, and technical documentation within a GMP-regulated environment. The role is predominantly office-based and offers the opportunity to become a key contributor to the company's future quality digitalisation initiatives.

About the Role

Reporting to the Senior Scientific Affairs Specialist, you will play a critical role in ensuring the quality and compliance of complementary medicine and functional food ingredients supplied throughout Australia and New Zealand.

Key responsibilities include:
  • Managing and maintaining Vendor Qualification Packages and Technical Information Packages.
  • Evaluating raw materials and reviewing technical documentation from a quality and compliance perspective.
  • Maintaining quality systems, SOPs, change controls, and non-conformance processes.
  • Ensuring manufacturer declarations, permits, certifications, and supporting documentation remain current and compliant.
  • Liaising with suppliers, regulatory bodies, and internal stakeholders regarding quality requirements.
  • Supporting vendor assurance activities and product compliance initiatives.
  • Assisting with the implementation of quality system improvements and future digitalisation projects.
About You

To be successful, you will bring: 
  • Experience working in Quality Assurance within the  complementary medicines industry.
  • Strong knowledge of GMP, PIC/S requirements, and TGA regulations.
  • Experience reviewing technical documentation, specifications, and supplier quality documentation.
  • A Bachelor's degree in a scientific discipline such as Chemistry, Food Science, Pharmaceutical Science, Naturopathy or a related field.
  • Exceptional attention to detail and documentation management skills.
  • Strong organisational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
What's on Offer?
  • Join a successful and growing Australian business with an excellent industry reputation.
  • Genuine work-life balance: standard hours around 8:45am–4:45pm and an early finish (3pm) every Friday
  • Opportunity to lead future quality system digitalisation projects.
  • Supportive and collaborative team culture.
  • Daily catered team lunches.
  • On-site parking available.
If you are passionate about quality, enjoy technical documentation and compliance, and want to join a business where your contribution will genuinely make an impact, we would love to hear from you. Should you wish to have a confidential conversation about this role, please email Grace Bitodi at gbitodi@onqrecruitment.com. au. Kindly note that application submitted via email will not be considered.

  • Create and implement scientific content dissemination plans.
  • Partner with Medical Affairs teams to optimise healthcare professional engagement.

  • Leverage platforms, email campaigns, websites and medical information channels.
  • Utilise customer insights, segmentation and performance data to improve engagement outcomes.
  • Manage external agencies and content vendors.
  • Develop dashboards and reporting to monitor campaign effectiveness and customer engagement.

You are a highly proactive and commercially aware omnichannel professional who enjoys working autonomously and influencing stakeholders in a complex matrix environment.

To be successful, you will bring:

Desirable
  • Knowledge of Medicines Australia Code and healthcare compliance frameworks.
